INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. A comparison using like or as
   B. A kind of song
   C. A long story
   D. A saying with no comparison

2. Which words signal a simile? (1 mark)
   A. is and are
   B. to and from
   C. but and or
   D. like and as

3. What does the Kiswahili proverb Kidole kimoja hakivunji chawa teach? (1 mark)
   A. One finger is very strong
   B. Lice are dangerous
   C. We need to work together
   D. Never use your hands

4. What does the English proverb Look before you leap teach? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the floor
   B. Think before you act
   C. Never move
   D. Jump quickly

5. What is the setting of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the writer
   B. Where and when it happens
   C. The last line
   D. The price

6. Which is a character in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The end
   B. A girl called Neema
   C. A shady tree
   D. The rainy season

7. What is a personal experience? (1 mark)
   A. Something that happened to you
   B. A rule
   C. A story from a book
   D. A number

8. Which question helps you plan an experience to tell? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the moon?
   B. How long is the ruler?
   C. What colour is the wall?
   D. Who was there?

9. What is a good first step when skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Close the book
   B. Skip the page
   C. Read every word carefully
   D. Read the title and headings

10. A seller buys mangoes for 300 shillings and sells them for 450 shillings. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. 300 shillings
   B. 450 shillings
   C. 750 shillings
   D. 150 shillings

11. What does a simple sentence have? (1 mark)
   A. Two subjects always
   B. No verb
   C. One subject and one predicate
   D. No capital

12. What are the two main parts of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Title and ending
   B. Noun and verb only
   C. Subject and predicate
   D. Capital and full stop

13. In front of means (1 mark)
   A. inside it
   B. behind it
   C. under it
   D. before something and facing it

14. The ball is touching the top of the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. on
   B. under
   C. behind
   D. outside

15. The bag is below the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. beside
   C. on
   D. between

16. Which is an example of caring for an animal? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving it without shelter
   B. Beating it
   C. Throwing stones at it
   D. Giving clean water every day

17. Why record yourself reciting? (1 mark)
   A. To delete your voice
   B. To stop practising
   C. To lose the poem
   D. To listen back and improve

18. What is a group of lines in a poem called? (1 mark)
   A. A chapter
   B. A stanza
   C. A sentence
   D. A paragraph

19. Which tense is used to tell a story about what happened? (1 mark)
   A. The past tense
   B. Only questions
   C. No tense
   D. Only the future

20. What should you do first when studying a picture for a story? (1 mark)
   A. Copy a story
   B. Write the ending
   C. Cover it
   D. Look at the whole picture

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Complete with a preposition: The cat sleeps ______ the bed. (2 marks)

22. Name three questions to ask yourself before telling a personal experience. (3 marks)

23. Give three questions you can ask when studying a picture. (3 marks)

24. Describe how you would scan a passage to find how much a box of mangoes costs. (4 marks)

25. Give three money words and their meanings. (3 marks)

26. Describe the steps in writing a story from a picture. (4 marks)

27. Explain what a story setting is. (2 marks)

28. Put in order: shillings the pays customer fifty (3 marks)

29. Explain why pace matters when reading a poem. (3 marks)

30. Give three steps for telling a story fluently. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — A comparison using like or as
   A simile compares two things using like or as.

2. D — like and as
   Similes use like or as.

3. C — We need to work together
   One finger cannot crush a louse, so cooperation is needed.

4. B — Think before you act
   It advises careful thought before doing something.

5. B — Where and when it happens
   Setting means place and time.

6. B — A girl called Neema
   Characters are the people or animals.

7. A — Something that happened to you
   A personal experience is an event you lived.

8. D — Who was there?
   Who, what, where, when, why and how help plan a story.

9. D — Read the title and headings
   The title tells the topic.

10. D — 150 shillings
   450 minus 300 is 150.

11. C — One subject and one predicate
   Simple sentences have one main idea.

12. C — Subject and predicate
   Every sentence has a subject and a predicate.

13. D — before something and facing it
   In front of shows the position ahead of something.

14. A — on
   On shows contact with the top.

15. A — under
   Under means below something.

16. D — Giving clean water every day
   Water and shelter meet its needs.

17. D — To listen back and improve
   Playback shows how to improve.

18. B — A stanza
   A stanza is a group of lines.

19. A — The past tense
   Stories about past events use the past.

20. D — Look at the whole picture
   First see the whole picture.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: under (or on, if it sleeps on top)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a preposition and one for a sentence that makes sense.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who was there, what happened, where, when, why, how did I feel.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each question.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who is there, where are they, what are they doing, why, what happens next.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Know that you are looking for the price, run your eyes over the text looking for numbers, stop at the number, read the sentence around it and check that it answers the question.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trade: buying and selling. Profit: money gained. Customer: person who buys. Price: cost of something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word with its meaning.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, ask who where and what, plan the characters, setting, problem and ending, write the story in order, and check it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: The setting is the place and time where the story happens.
   Working / marking points: One mark for place and one for time.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: The customer pays fifty shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the words in order, one for the capital and one for the full stop.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: A pace that is too fast makes words unclear, and one that is too slow loses interest. A good pace helps listeners follow and feel the mood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of three ideas.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Know the story well, speak clearly, keep a steady pace, change your voice for characters, look at the audience, end with the lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.
